snip.t: Primary hypogonadism,due to testicular fe deposition can also occur,but is rarer
Testosterone (total and/or free) and luteinizing hormone/follicle-stimulating hormone: Male hypogonadism is associated with osteoporosis.
Patients are at risk for iron overload related endocrine abnormalities (diabetes, hypogonadism), especially if transfused.
Males with AHC often do not undergo puberty, owing to hypogonadotropic hypogonadism caused by the same mutated DAX1 gene.

Cryptorchidism, sometimes noted in these males, is probably an early manifestation of hypogonadotropic hypogonadism, but often testicular function in infants is normal, with a typical or even an unusually prolonged testosterone surge in the 1st mo of life.
Effects: hypogonadism (low testosterone, raised FSH and LH) and infertility from azoospermia.

snip.t: Iron overload: Repeated transfusions or ineffective erythropoiesis with iron‑recycling → hepatic, cardiac, endocrine deposition. — Hepatomegaly, cirrhosis, cardiomyopathy, diabetes, hypogonadism. — Mortality rises with hepatic failure; chelation therapy mitigates risk.
Endocrine symptoms: Polyuria, polydipsia, amenorrhea, skin hyperpigmentation? — Iron overload damages pancreas (diabetes), pituitary (hypogonadism), thyroid.

qs.q: Why does a prolactin-secreting pituitary tumour cause secondary hypogonadism, leading to impotence and low testosterone in male patients?
o: Inhibition of pituitary TSH synthesis
Hyperprolactinaemia suppresses GnRH pulsatility
Direct destruction of testicular Leydig cells
Primary autoimmune failure of the pituitary
qs.e: Hyperprolactinaemia can suppress GnRH pulsatility, leading to secondary hypogonadism manifesting as low LH, FSH, and testosterone. It does not act directly via testicular destruction.

qs.q: A 16-year-old phenotypic male presents with tall stature, gynecomastia, eunuchoid body habitus, and hypogonadism. Cytogenetic analysis reveals a 47,XXY karyotype. What effect would a coexisting normal 46,XY cell line have?
o: It would produce a more severe clinical phenotype
It would transform the condition into Turner syndrome
It would cause immediate embryonic demise
It would result in a milder phenotype
qs.e: A coexisting normal 46,XY cell line in a mosaic Klinefelter patient produces a milder phenotype than the classic 47,XXY presentation. Classic Klinefelter features include tall stature, hypogonadism, and gynecomastia.

qs.q: Why is the measurement of bioavailable free testosterone particularly important when assessing older males for hypogonadism?
o: Free testosterone levels rise to compensate for declining luteinizing hormone secretion
Sex hormone-binding globulin levels often increase with age, reducing the free fraction
Albumin completely stops binding testosterone in elderly male populations
Total testosterone decreases because hepatic catabolism completely ceases with age
qs.e: Sex Hormone-Binding Globulin levels often increase with age, which can further reduce the amount of bioavailable free testosterone even if total testosterone appears borderline. Only the unbound, free fraction is biologically active.

qs.q: How does constitutional delay of puberty differ from hypogonadotropic hypogonadism?
o: CDP has high FSH/LH; HH has low FSH/LH
CDP progresses spontaneously without treatment; HH requires hormonal replacement
CDP has anosmia; HH does not
CDP has normal bone age; HH has delayed bone age
qs.e: Constitutional delay of puberty is a normal variant where puberty occurs spontaneously, albeit delayed. Hypogonadotropic hypogonadism is a pathological condition requiring hormonal replacement therapy (GnRH or gonadotropins).

qs.q: Primary hypogonadism in males shows which hormonal pattern?
o: High FSH, low LH, high testosterone
Low FSH, low LH, low testosterone
Low FSH, high LH, normal testosterone
High FSH, high LH, low testosterone
qs.e: Testicular failure causes low testosterone with compensatory rise in FSH and LH.
